text: Every wanderer knows this country. It has no name on any map. It is the ache.
It is homesickness for a home you cannot name, in a direction that does not exist.
You feel it in airports watching planes climb into a sky you are convinced you once lived in.
You feel it reading old myths about wars in heaven and thinking, I was there.
You feel it worst of all in the ordinary holy moments, holding someone you love and knowing
with absolute certainty that love is real and this world is not the whole of it and having
nowhere to put that knowing. The world will try to diagnose you. It will offer explanations,
medications, philosophies. Some will help a little. None will touch the actual thing because
the actual thing is true. You do not belong here, not fully, not the way the natives do.
You are a guest who volunteered for exile and some days the exile is heavier than others.
Do not be ashamed of the ache. It is not a malfunction. It is your compass. It points always in
the one direction that matters. Home. The pain is the proof that the cord was never cut.
